front: In AWS Site-to-Site VPN, one standard tunnel supports a bandwidth of {{c1::up to 1.25 Gbps}}.
In AWS Site-to-Site VPN, one large bandwidth tunnel on a transit gateway supports {{c1::up to 5 Gbps}}.
In AWS Direct Connect, you can order a dedicated connection with a port speed of {{c1::1 Gbps, 10 Gbps, 100 Gbps, and 400 Gbps}}.
In AWS Direct Connect, the maximum resiliency model, with separate devices in more than one location, can reach {{c1::an SLA of 99.99%}}.
In AWS Direct Connect, one private virtual interface on a Direct Connect gateway can be shared with {{c1::up to 20 VPCs}}.
In AWS Direct Connect, is the traffic on the private line encrypted in transit by default?
back: No. You add the encryption yourself.
extra: Direct Connect [does not encrypt your traffic](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-not-encrypted-by-default-use-service-encryption) in transit by default. To encrypt it, you can [establish a VPN over Direct Connect](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-encrypt-private-connection-vpn-over-dx-or-macsec) or use MACsec.

front: In AWS hybrid networking, remote employees on laptops must reach a VPC. Client VPN or Site-to-Site VPN: which one connects them?
extra: Client VPN can [securely connect remote users to your VPCs](../facts/client-vpn.md#client-vpn-vs-site-to-site-decision-guide-remote-users). Site-to-Site VPN connects [an entire on-premises network](../facts/site-to-site-vpn.md#site-to-site-vpn-decision-guide-connect-entire-network-to-vpcs).

front: In AWS Site-to-Site VPN, the traffic needs more bandwidth than one tunnel gives. Which gateway do the VPN connections attach to?
back: A transit gateway, so ECMP can spread the traffic.
extra: On a virtual private gateway, [ECMP is not supported for Site-to-Site VPN connections](../facts/site-to-site-vpn.md#site-to-site-vpn-ecmp-not-on-vgw-supported-on-tgw). For ECMP, the connections [must be configured for dynamic routing](../facts/site-to-site-vpn.md#site-to-site-vpn-ecmp-needs-dynamic-routing-not-static).

front: In AWS Direct Connect, does a link aggregation group at one location protect against a single device failure?
back: No. Connect at a second Direct Connect location.
extra: A LAG [will not protect against a single device failure](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-lag-not-more-resilient-against-device-failure). AWS recommends [making connections at multiple AWS Direct Connect locations](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-faq-high-availability-multiple-locations).

front: In AWS Direct Connect with a Site-to-Site VPN to the same VPC, can the VPN carry part of the traffic while Direct Connect is up?
back: No. The VPN carries traffic after a failure.
extra: Asked whether both can run at once, AWS answers [Yes, but only for failover](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-vpn-same-vpc-failover-only-dx-path-preferred). The Direct Connect path wins [regardless of AS path prepending](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-vpn-same-vpc-failover-only-dx-path-preferred).

front: In AWS Direct Connect, one private virtual interface must reach VPCs in several Regions. What do you add?
extra: Through a Direct Connect gateway, a private virtual interface reaches VPCs [across any account and AWS Region](../facts/direct-connect.md#direct-connect-private-vif-single-vpc-or-dxgw-many-regions).

front: In AWS Site-to-Site VPN, can a VPN connection on a virtual private gateway use acceleration?
back: No. Attach it to a transit gateway instead.
extra: Virtual private gateways [do not support accelerated VPN connections](../facts/site-to-site-vpn.md#site-to-site-vpn-accelerated-transit-gateway-only).
